findings.reason: the enumeration understates the host-layer edit by two declarations, and as written the section's own test cannot pass, so a builder would either land a failing gate or hunt for the missing two lines the plan never names.
findings.text: §19 states "The host layer `~/Code/dotfiles/reckon/flight.yaml` still carries `backends: codex-luna: {}` and `codex-astra: {}`" and counts "four lines of configuration outside this repository", but that host layer also declares `backends.claude-opus: {}` (line 484) and `backends.claude-haiku: {}` (line 500), each commented "Name declaration only: keeps the lane's derived claude-opus entry live in the resolved config"; §19's own Why states "the lane expansion in `reckon/flight.py` keeps any combined name some layer declares", and its done-when resolves *this repository's* flight (which merges over the host layer) and requires no entry carrying `derived_from` — so a coordinator removing only the two codex lines leaves two derived entries alive and the section's measure unmet

findings.reason: the ordering the plan itself calls load-bearing exists only in prose, so a coordinator dispatching from the roadmap can strand Jev with one candidate per lane exactly as §18's Why warns.
findings.text: §19 states "This section runs after §17 and §18" and §18's Why states that "Retiring the combined names (§19) before this lands would leave Jev offered only each lane's default model", but `plan-section-depends-on` (line 22) holds only `s4`, `s10` and `s14`, so no `s18`/`s19` edge encodes that order and the roadmap can offer §19 ahead of §18
